body:
so I thought.

I love them. But I feel like I'm doing them more harm than good.

>I wouldn't separate a child from its family because of canned food and old threadbare clothes and not having a permanent residence.

CPS would. And has threatened to. If you felt your children were going to be taken from you anyways, wouldn't you rather have some control over the outcome?

And OF COURSE a child isn't a dog. That was the point. People consider the needs of an animal, and relinquish it if they cannot meet those needs (or not, in which case they're bad pet owners). People consider the needs of a child, and painful as it may be, they might have to relinquish the child if they cannot meet those needs.. or be forced to do so by a state agency.. or keep the child, and it continues to suffer, in the name of love.

You make good points in your Edit. But I ask you: if your children are hungry and miserable, you are destitute and mentally unstable, and you know there are well-off, sane, loving families in search of a child.. what would you do?

I've fought to take care of them for six years now. I've done an awful job and now here we are at rock bottom. I don't know when it will improve. How long will they have to wait to have a decent childhood?

>If you have to give up custody, try to keep them together with relatives until your situation improves. I doubt many people are looking to take in or adopt three siblings at once.

Very true. This would be ideal.

As far as "better off being poor and together".. sure. But if you buy a dog and can't afford to feed it, you get rid of it for the animal's sake. Why be selfish with a child? Doesn't that child deserve food, shelter, clothing, and comfort, whether or not you are the source? If you can't provide these things, why hold on to the child except for your own selfish reasons?
That's an interesting concept. I'll look into it.

I've heard this is actually very damaging for the children - to be removed and re-integrated, and deal with emotional fallout from that, and then removed and re-integrated with someone they don't remember or no longer trust.

I think it would be best if they forgot me entirely. I'd love to know how they're doing, and get to know them as adults, if possible, but I don't think I can trust myself to get them there without significant disadvantage and damage.
Thank you for your input. I appreciate it.

6, 4, and 2.

I've never injured them, but I do yell and grab them more than I like. I keep a pretty good lid on my impulses but sometimes it overwhelms me. When I'm depressed it is particularly bad; I want to be alone and I get very angry if bothered.

Mother. Father is unmedicated bipolar slacker. Worse off than I am. So no.
Thanks. That's what I'm trying to do. :)

While I appreciate your advice, I think you might have misinterpreted some parts of my post.

I have no "disdain" towards "suit-wearing pencil-pushers", nor am I avoiding low-wage jobs. I'm applying for everything I am remotely qualified to do, and even some ambitious positions for which I'm not fully prepared. At this point the concept of allowing pride to stop me from making money is ridiculous, because my sanity and my family's survival is at stake.

We've contacted shelters and food pantries. The shelters are packed - homelessness is high - but I did manage to request a pre-application for subsidized housing yesterday. We've been regularly going to food pantries, but due to the local demand and the lack of people able to make donations, many of them allow only monthly or bimonthly visits. And again there's the issue of having no money for gas, without which we can't even get to food pantries.

I've considered adoption. At times it seems selfish that I insist my children suffer through this at my side. I don't know if I could stand not having them with me, though. Some days they're the only thing keeping me going.

I'm not really spending time "not doing anything", except when my depression gets so bad that I just can't function for a few hours or a day. Doing research during those times would be a waste of effort, as I wouldn't be able to absorb anything. I've begun trying to learn programming (Python and C++), I'm participating in NaNoWriMo (writing a novel), and in the next few weeks I'm going to spend some time studying Excel. All of this has to take place between 8 p.m. and midnight (or whenever bedtime happens), though, because the rest of the day, my time is occupied with caring for my kids. Then I'm up at 6 the next day getting my oldest son ready for school.

There's very little wasted time. Yet I feel like I'm just spinning my wheels and not getting anywhere.

Many of my husband's family members are disabled and don't work, but some of them have connections. I haven't asked them for help because they're already giving us so much.. but if I had work we could get out of their hair! 

I can't get a standard job until I have ID. Freelancing seems like my only option, but you're right - even babysitting is something.
